issue.title: [Windows][gfx1201] torch 2.12.0+rocm7.14.1 and +rocm10.0.0: kernels fail with hipErrorInvalidValue after any SDPA call; +rocm7.14.0 is fine
issue.body:
## Summary

On Windows with a Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201), the PyTorch wheels `torch==2.12.0+rocm7.14.1`
(from `https://repo.amd.com/rocm/whl-multi-arch/`) and `torch==2.12.0+rocm10.0.0`
(from `https://stable.repo.amd.com/rocm/whl-next/`) exhibit the same regression:
once `torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention` has been called (any backend
selected by default), certain unrelated kernels afterwards fail with
`AcceleratorError: CUDA error: invalid argument` (`hipErrorInvalidValue`).

`torch==2.12.0+rocm7.14.0` from the same multi-arch index, same machine, same driver,
same Python, passes every test. Note that 7.14.0 and 7.14.1 report the *same*
`torch.version.hip` (`7.14.60850`), so the difference is in the torch build, not the
HIP runtime.

Disabling the flash / mem-efficient SDPA backends
(`torch.backends.cuda.enable_flash_sdp(False)`, `enable_mem_efficient_sdp(False)`)
before any SDPA call makes all subsequent kernels succeed.

Practical impact: ComfyUI 0.34 crashes on a plain SDXL text-encoder forward pass
(SDPA followed by a dtype cast) on 7.14.1 and 10.0.0; works on 7.14.0.

## Environment

- GPU: AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 32 GB (gfx1201); iGPU Ryzen 7 5700G (gfx90c) present,
  hidden via `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0`
- OS: Windows 10 (x64)
- Driver: AMD Software PRO Edition 26.10.36 (260727a-203347C)
- Python: 3.13.15 (python.org)
- `torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0)`: `gcnArchName='gfx1201', major=12, minor=0, total_memory=32624MB`
- Failing wheels:
  - `torch==2.12.0+rocm7.14.1`, `torchvision==0.27.0+rocm7.14.1`, `torchaudio==2.11.0+rocm7.14.1`
    installed with `torch[device-gfx1201]` from `https://repo.amd.com/rocm/whl-multi-arch/`
    (`rocm-sdk-core 7.14.1`, `torch.version.hip == '7.14.60850'`)
  - `torch==2.12.0+rocm10.0.0`, `torchvision==0.27.0+rocm10.0.0`, `torchaudio==2.11.0+rocm10.0.0`
    installed with `torch[device-gfx1201]` from `https://stable.repo.amd.com/rocm/whl-next/`
    (`rocm-sdk-core 10.0.0`, `torch.version.hip == '7.15.26333'`)
- Working wheel: `torch==2.12.0+rocm7.14.0` from `https://repo.amd.com/rocm/whl-multi-arch/`
  (`rocm-sdk-core 7.14.0`, `torch.version.hip == '7.14.60850'`)

`AMD_SERIALIZE_KERNEL=1` does not change the outcome. (`AMD_SERIALIZE_KERNEL=3` is
rejected by these builds: "valid values are 0 or 1".)

## Reproducer

`test_order.py`:

```python
import sys, torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
from torch.nn.attention import sdpa_kernel, SDPBackend

def t(name, fn):
    try:
        fn(); torch.cuda.synchronize(); print("OK   ", name)
    except Exception as e:
        print("FAIL ", name, "|", str(e).splitlines()[0])

mode = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "flash_first"
if mode == "no_flash":
    torch.backends.cuda.enable_flash_sdp(False)
    torch.backends.cuda.enable_mem_efficient_sdp(False)

q = torch.randn(1, 20, 77, 64, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16)

def math_sdpa():
    with sdpa_kernel(SDPBackend.MATH):
        return F.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, q, q)

t("e4m3 cast (before any sdpa)", lambda: torch.randn(1280, 1280, device="cuda").to(torch.float8_e4m3fn))
t("MATH sdpa (before default)",  math_sdpa)
t("default sdpa",                lambda: F.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, q, q))
t("e4m3 cast (after sdpa)",      lambda: torch.randn(1280, 1280, device="cuda").to(torch.float8_e4m3fn))
t("softmax fp32 (after sdpa)",   lambda: torch.softmax(torch.randn(20, 77, 77, device="cuda"), -1))
t("linear fp32 (after sdpa)",    lambda: F.linear(torch.randn(77, 1280, device="cuda"), torch.randn(1280, 1280, device="cuda")))
```

Run:
set HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0
python test_order.py flash_first
python test_order.py no_flash


## Results

`torch 2.12.0+rocm7.14.1` and `2.12.0+rocm10.0.0`, `flash_first`:

OK e4m3 cast (before any sdpa)
OK MATH sdpa (before default)
OK default sdpa
FAIL e4m3 cast (after sdpa) | CUDA error: invalid argument
OK softmax fp32 (after sdpa)
OK linear fp32 (after sdpa)


Same wheels, `no_flash`: all six OK.

`torch 2.12.0+rocm7.14.0`, `flash_first`: all six OK.

A second script that runs SDPA with each backend in turn shows the same pattern on the
failing wheels: `default` OK, then `MATH` FAIL, `FLASH_ATTENTION` OK,
`EFFICIENT_ATTENTION` OK, then `float32 -> float8_e4m3fn` FAIL while
`float32 -> float8_e5m2` OK. In isolation (no SDPA in the process) every one of those
operations, including the e4m3fn cast, succeeds on all three wheels — the failure only
appears for kernels launched *after* an SDPA call while the flash/mem-efficient
backends are enabled.

## Expected

Kernels launched after an SDPA call should not fail; behaviour should match
`2.12.0+rocm7.14.0`.

## Notes

- The failure is deterministic (reproduced ~10 times across the two failing wheels).
- Triton (`triton-windows 3.7.1.post27`) is *not* involved: the same result with it
  uninstalled, and `triton.jit` kernels themselves run fine on all three wheels.
- Happy to run additional diagnostics (e.g. `AMD_LOG_LEVEL`, specific env flags) on request.
- This round of debugging was done by Claude Fable 5.1. It's difficult to understand for me. 😅

labels.description: Indicates an issue has been assigned for investigation.

issue.display_title: [Windows][gfx1201] torch 2.12.0+rocm7.14.1 and +rocm10.0.0: kernels fail with hipErrorInvalidValue after any SDPA call; +rocm7.14.0 is fine

comments.body: Hey @overdoignism, can you try this reproducer out on the latest nightlies? There was a HIP/AOTriton hash version mismatch which also manifested as `hipErrorInvalidValue` and was only recently resolved - I'm curious to see if this is the same and a test on latest would help confirm.

Confirmed fixed on the latest nightly. Same machine (R9700 / gfx1201, Win10, driver 26.10.36, Python 3.13.15), fresh venv:

- torch 2.15.0a0+rocm10.1.0a20260908, torchvision 0.30.0a0, torchaudio 2.11.0.3
- rocm-sdk-core / libraries / device-gfx1201 10.1.0a20260908

`test_order.py flash_first`: all 6 OK. `test_order.py no_flash`: all 6 OK.
`test_sdpa.py`: default / MATH / FLASH / EFFICIENT all OK; float8_e4m3fn and e5m2 casts OK.

One caveat: the nightly is torch 2.15 whereas the failing wheels were 2.12, so torch itself also changed — but the pass is consistent with the HIP/AOTriton hash mismatch you described. Will re-check when a stable 2.12/10.0.x wheel with the fix lands. Thanks!

You can find torch==2.12.0 wheels over on on nightly.repo.amd.com/rocm/whl-next/. For example, https://nightly.repo.amd.com/rocm/pytorch/whl-next/torch/torch-2.12.0%2Brocm10.2.0a20260914-cp312-cp312-win_amd64.whl.
Closing this out as the issue has been resolved in latest nightlies. Feel free to leave a comment if you're still running into this/similar issues.
